senses.gloss: the tool you use every day
gloss_distractors: a tool you are still testing
the person who leads a team
senses.definition: The tool you actually use every day, rather than a backup or one you are still testing.
senses.caution: Only say it about a tool you really use, because people will ask what its problems are. It is casual, so avoid it in formal written recommendations.
senses.example: Claude is my daily driver, I keep the others around for the one or two jobs they are better at.

cues.text: A colleague asks which of the three coding assistants you actually reach for, not which ones you have tried.
In a tooling review you want to separate the editor most engineers live in from the ones installed once and forgotten.
A friend with three bicycles is asked which one he rides to work and which he keeps for weekends.
You keep a good camera for holidays and photograph everything else on your phone, and you want the term for the phone.

distractors: A tool bought and never installed.
A spare kept in a drawer in case the main one fails.
The version of a product given to reviewers before release.
The tool a company has standardised on and pays for, whether or not anyone enjoys using it.
A product used only for demonstrations, set up carefully so nothing goes wrong on stage.
